[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a class of deep neural networks, most commonly applied to analyzing visual imagery. Unlike standard feedforward neural networks, CNNs use spatial relationships to reduce the number of parameters to learn, making them highly efficient for image classification, object detection, and segmentation."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of a CNN"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Convolutional Layer: The fundamental building block of a CNN, which uses filters (kernels) to perform convolution operations, extracting feature maps like edges, corners, and textures."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pooling Layer: Used to downsample the feature maps, reducing the spatial dimensions, computational complexity, and the number of parameters (e.g., Max Pooling)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fully Connected Layer: Flattens the final feature maps into a 1-dimensional vector to output class probabilities using activation functions like Softmax."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing a Simple CNN in Python"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a standard implementation of a Convolutional Neural Network using the TensorFlow and Keras libraries for image classification."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models

# Build the CNN architecture
model = models.Sequential([
    layers.Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation='relu', input_shape=(28, 28, 1)),
    layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation='relu'),
    layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    layers.Flatten(),
    layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

# Compile the model
model.compile(optimizer='adam',
              loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
              metrics=['accuracy'])"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"CNNs revolutionize computer vision by automatically detecting spatial hierarchies of features. By combining convolutional layers, pooling operations, and dense layers, they achieve state-of-the-art performance on various visual tasks."}]
